title: How many must bend under a door at the mean height?
description: A family's six heights are added, divided by six, and compared with each member. Some members are taller than the mean, so a door of that height does not suit them. Keeko doubts this and thinks a door at the mean height fits everyone.
teaching_notes: One idea: the mean is a fair share, so some values always lie above it, and a door that must fit everyone is set by the maximum. Watch for students who use the mean for every decision.

source: A family's heights are 169, 173, 155, 165, 160 and 164 cm. A
video_script.why: The child sees that the mean is not always the right measure for a decision.
video_script.substitution: The six heights of the family from the book, with a door as tall as their mean.
video_script.anchor: A family of six members of different heights standing beside a door made as tall as their average height
video_script.wrong_answer: a door at the mean height fits everyone
video_script.wrong_move: Treats the mean as a safe height for everyone because it is a fair share, forgetting that some members are taller than it.
video_script.payoff_line: Three members must bend, and the door must be taller than the maximum.

final_answer.value: 3 members must bend; the door must be taller than 173 cm
final_answer.spoken: three members must bend and the door must be taller than one hundred and seventy three centimetres

names.Jia: the child whose family's heights are measured

maths_rules: taller than 164.33: 165, 169 and 173, so 3 of the 6 members
a door that fits everyone must be taller than 173
video_script.design: One family of six and one door. The mean height is drawn as a line across the door, and the three taller members cross it.

beats.on_screen: small title card From your book; a family of six standing in a row of different heights next to a door

marks.m1: the title card From your book appears
marks.m2: the six members appear in a row
marks.m4: a question mark appears over the door

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book about Jia's family.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The family has six members, and every height is measured.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A door is made exactly as tall as the average height of the family.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>How many members must bend to pass through, and how tall should the door be?

beats.on_screen: the family and the door stay on the board

marks.m1: Keeko sits at the corner of the board as the child

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: the heights added in a column with a division by the number of members; a tallest member marked

marks.m1: the heights are added and divided by the count
marks.m3: the tallest member is labelled maximum

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Add all the heights and divide by how many there are.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The result is called the mean.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>The greatest height in the group is called the maximum.

beats.on_screen: Given: heights 169, 173, 155, 165, 160, 164 cm; door at the mean height

marks.m1: the first three heights are written
marks.m2: the last three heights are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, the family has six heights. The first is one hundred and sixty nine. The second is one hundred and seventy three. <bookmark mark='m3'/>The third is one hundred and fifty five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The fourth is one hundred and sixty five. The fifth is one hundred and sixty. The sixth is one hundred and sixty four.

beats.on_screen: To find: members taller than the door; the height of a door that fits everyone

marks.m1: the two questions are written one under the other

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find who must bend, and how tall a door that fits everyone must be.

marks.m1: the six heights line up in a column
marks.m2: the total 986 cm is written under them

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, add the six heights, because the mean starts with the total.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The total is nine hundred and eighty six centimetres.

marks.m2: a line at 164.33 cm is drawn across the door

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, divide the total by six, because there are six members.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Divide nine hundred and eighty six by six. The mean is about one hundred and sixty four point three three centimetres.

beats.on_screen: taller than 164.33: 165, 169, 173; the other three are shorter

marks.m1: each height is compared with the line on the door
marks.m2: 165, 169 and 173 light up above the line
marks.m3: the three members who bend are outlined

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, find who is taller than the mean. They would hit the top of the door.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>One is one hundred and sixty five. Another is one hundred and sixty nine. The last is one hundred and seventy three.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Three of the six members must bend.

beats.on_screen: maximum = 173 cm; the door must be taller than the maximum

marks.m1: the tallest member is marked 173 cm
marks.m2: the door is redrawn above the tallest member

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, a door must fit everyone, so compare it with the maximum.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The maximum is one hundred and seventy three centimetres. The door must be taller than that, with a little room to spare.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 3 members must bend; door taller than 173 cm
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Three members must bend, and the door must be taller than the maximum.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>The door must be taller than one hundred and seventy three centimetres.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the family and the door
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: a door at the mean height fits everyone; the three taller members bump the top and the doubt is struck through

marks.m1: the doubt appears as a bubble
marks.m2: the three taller members bump the top of the door and the bubble is struck through
marks.m3: the maximum line is drawn above the door

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Keeko thinks a door at the mean height fits everyone, because the mean is fair to all.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>But a fair share is not a safe height. Some members always stand above the mean.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>A door must clear the tallest member, so let the question choose the measure.
